subject: Re: ACME discovery — feature parity & next tests (streaming, tool calls, structured outputs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Keane <jordan@acme.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: ACME discovery — feature parity & next tests (streaming, tool calls, structured outputs)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can validate the parity items you mentioned with the engineering team: 

Call recap:
- Primary goal: replace current inference layer (hyperscaler API) for customer-facing assistants while matching feature set (streaming responses, tool/function calling, structured JSON outputs) and improving cost/latency.
- Must-haves for POC: streaming token-by-token output, support for function/tool calls with opaque tool payloads, and stable structured outputs for downstream parsing.
- Non-functional: SLA/uptime expectations, audit logs, and data residency for EU customers (we discussed Dedicated or Private later).

Proposed next tests (short and actionable):
1) Streaming test — we’ll run a side-by-side: Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI vs Redwood streaming with identical prompts and long-context multi-turn chats (we’ll log latency and token arrival time).
2) Tool calling — reproduce your current tool-call payloads (one sync webhook, one async job kickoff) and validate our function-calling contract and error semantics.
3) Structured outputs — run the same schema-driven generation (order JSONs) and compare parse success rate and regression examples.

Attached is a feature-parity matrix I filled out from today’s notes (redwood-feature-parity-matrix.xlsx). If you can:
- Share your sample prompts and a small set of test prompts (10–20) for each test above.
- Confirm who on your side will own the technical POC (call out an engineer).

I’ll loop in Rishi (cc’d) to propose resources and a timeline once we have the test prompts. Proposed timeline: kickoff early next week, 3–5 day test runs per vector, then a short results review.

Thanks — looking forward to making this concrete.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-feature-parity-matrix.xlsx
From: Jordan Keane <jordan@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara@acme-devs.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: ACME discovery — feature parity & next tests (streaming, tool calls, structured outputs)

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. Sara will lead the POC on our side. We can provide sample prompts and the tool webhook payloads. Quick clarifications before we kick off:

- For streaming: we care about token arrival time (we currently see jitter at ~150–250ms per token with our current setup). Can you capture per-token latency in the test harness?
- For function calls: we need guarantee on deterministic serialization for our tool inputs (order of keys matters for downstream systems). Does Redwood preserve key order in the function call payload?
- For structured outputs: we’ll include a few known edge-case prompts that have caused parsing regressions before.

Sara — can you share the sample prompts and the webhook payloads by tomorrow EOD? Also tagging procurement to start the paperwork once we have the technical green light.

Jordan
Director of Product, ACME Corp
jordan@acme.com

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME discovery — feature parity & next tests (streaming, tool calls, structured outputs)

On Tue, Feb 15, 2027 at 9:12 AM Jordan Keane <jordan@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. Sara will lead the POC on our side.

Hi all — Sara here (Engineering Lead). I’m attaching a small corpus and two webhook examples. We’ve anonymized the data. Links: sample-prompts.json (10 prompts), webhook-sync.json, webhook-async.json.

Notes for Redwood POC team:
- Streaming: measure token arrival times and provide raw timing logs so we can plot jitter vs token index. Ideally include a small script we can run to reproduce the same client-side behavior.
- Function calls: our tooling expects canonical JSON (UTF-8, stable key ordering for signature verification). If Redwood serializes objects differently, we need an explanation of how best to canonicalize or a config option to get stable serialization.
- Structured outputs: we’ll validate by running our existing parser and giving you the parse-fail examples. We expect >95% parse success for the schema set we attached.

We can start the tests as soon as you confirm the infra resources and a short test plan. If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute tech sync (engineer-to-engineer) tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Engineering Lead, ACME Corp
sara@acme-devs.com

Attachments: sample-prompts.json (link), webhook-sync.json (link), webhook-async.json (link)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@acme-devs.com>, Jordan Keane <jordan@acme.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Feb 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME discovery — feature parity & next tests (streaming, tool calls, structured outputs)

Thanks Sara — really helpful. Quick plan and owners from our side: 

Plan (owners):
- Test harness & scripts for streaming measurements (Priyom) — we’ll capture per-token timestamps and produce CSVs with token_index, server_recv_ts, server_send_ts, client_receive_ts.
- Function-call contract runbook (Rishi) — confirm serialization guarantees and provide recommended canonicalization approach if needed.
- Structured-output eval (Marissa + Priyom) — run your corpus through Redwood and share parse success rates + failure cases.

Next steps:
1) Priyom will reach out with a short conftest and the streaming script by EOD today.
2) Rishi will document serialization behavior and a recommended approach for deterministic signing by tomorrow.
3) We’ll run initial 3-day test window starting Thursday and share interim results by Monday next week.

If this works, Jordan/procurement — can you confirm a lightweight MSA or a POC addendum (we’ve done an expedited POC contract before)? Happy to loop legal/procurement once you confirm.

Folks — I’ve attached the demo recording from our streaming proof-of-concept (streaming-demo-recording.mp4) and the parity matrix. We’ll update the matrix as tests complete.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
